evidence: Built manifest_tool.py, a PO03-MANIFEST-v1 generator/verifier pair with a working-tree source and a git source over an immutable commit. Ran python3 -I -m unittest discover over the unit subtree: 25 tests, OK, exit 0, captured verbatim in evidence/test-run.txt. Generated evidence/MANIFEST-head.txt from git commit 7771421daa577c27ad780bd8509f891d02473457 (3 artifacts, 28124 bytes) and re-verified it: PO03_MANIFEST_PASS exit 0. Four adversarial mutations of that manifest were then executed and captured in evidence/cli-demo.txt: deleting an entry produced UNCOVERED_FILE path=FINDINGS.md plus trailer mismatches (exit 1), flipping one hex digit produced HASH_MISMATCH path=manifest_tool.py (exit 1), inflating a byte count by one produced BYTE_MISMATCH path=test_manifest_tool.py (exit 1). An entry omission with a forged self-consistent trailer still fails because source enumeration and not the trailer is authoritative.
falsifiable_hypothesis: Every committed PO-03 artifact is covered by a manifest entry with a matching hash and byte count, and any gap fails closed.
limitations: Coverage is only defined relative to a declared source: a git-source manifest cannot see an unstaged file, so a producer that never stages a file yields a manifest complete against the commit and incomplete against the working tree; test_unstaged_file_is_invisible_to_a_git_source_but_caught_by_a_directory_source asserts this asymmetry rather than assuming it.

The line-oriented PO03-MANIFEST-v1 format cannot represent paths containing newline, carriage return, NUL or the two-space field separator; such paths are refused as UNSAFE_PATH rather than mangled, so those artifacts cannot be counted at all.

An earlier draft of the command-line demonstration used sed 's/^0/1/', which mutated nothing because no hash began with 0 and therefore falsely showed a PASS; the demonstration was rewritten to flip a hex digit programmatically and the corrected run is what is committed.
